title: Cost, speed and model routing
hook: One big model for everything is the expensive default. Route, cache, and trim instead.

useCase.title: 100,000 tickets a day and a rising bill
useCase.story: The assistant works, but cost and delay grow with volume. Most questions are easy repeats. A few are hard.

approaches.name: One biggest model for everything
approaches.what: Send every request to the strongest model.
approaches.example: Every "hello" is priced like a hard case.

approaches.name: Model routing
approaches.what: A cheap model handles easy requests and escalates when unsure.
approaches.example: FAQ goes to a small model. A complex complaint goes to a large one.

approaches.name: Caching
approaches.what: Reuse answers or repeated prompt parts.
approaches.avoidWhen: Every question is unique or personal.
approaches.example: "Opening hours?" is answered once and reused.

approaches.name: Shorter prompts, smarter retrieval
approaches.example: Send the three best passages, not thirty.

approaches.name: A small model trained for one job
approaches.what: Train a small model to copy a large one on a narrow task.
approaches.example: The email categorizer from the first stop.

approaches.name: Batch processing
approaches.what: Run non-urgent work later, in bulk, often at lower prices.
approaches.example: Nightly summaries of the day's tickets.

challenge.question: About 70% of questions are simple repeats. What is the best cost move?

options.text: Route by difficulty, cache repeats, and trim prompts
options.why: Repeats cost almost nothing, easy questions use a cheap model, and only hard ones reach the big one.

options.text: Switch everything to the smallest model
options.why: Hard cases get shallow, wrong answers.

options.text: Keep the biggest model and negotiate a better price later
options.why: You keep paying hard-case prices for easy questions.

options.text: Fine-tune a small model right away
options.why: Can pay off at steady high volume, but routing and caching are quicker wins first.

bestCase.title: Route by difficulty, cache repeats, trim prompts
bestCase.example: "What are your opening hours?" is served from the cache in milliseconds. Simple questions go to a small model. Only the tricky minority reach the large model. The bill drops while quality on hard cases holds.

worstCase.title: Biggest model for everything, or smallest for everything
worstCase.example: Every "hi" costs as much as a deep analysis and answers feel slow. Or you swap in the tiny model everywhere and hard complaints get shallow, wrong answers.

steps.label: Question in
steps.goes: The same question was asked 400 times today.

steps.label: Cache check
steps.goes: Seen before? Return the saved answer instantly.
steps.goesWrong: There is no cache. Every repeat pays for a full model call.

steps.label: Difficulty router
steps.goes: Easy goes to a small model. Hard goes to a large model.

steps.label: Chosen model
steps.goes: The small model answers in under a second.

steps.label: Log cost and quality
steps.goes: Track price and accuracy for each route.

takeaway: Match model size to task difficulty, and never pay twice for the same answer.
